intro.data: Two steps: from the form, BUILD a record that bundles the name and age; then PROJECT the name back out. The whole round must return the original name. One builder packs the fields in order; the other swaps them. One projection reads the first field; the other misreads. Only the faithful pair survives — picking by color won't.
intro.alchemy: Two steps: from the seed, COMBINE a compound bundling salt and sulfur; then DRAW the salt back out. The whole round must return the original salt. One combiner orders the parts; the other swaps them. One draw reads the first part; the other misreads.
intro.spellcraft: Two steps: from the caster, WEAVE a blend bundling light and heat; then DRAW the light back out. The whole round must return the original light. One weaver orders the parts; the other swaps them. One draw reads the first part; the other misreads.
intro.abstract: Build ⟨f,g⟩ : X→A×B, then apply π₁ : A×B→A; the composite must recover the A-component. A swapped pairing or a mis-projection returns the wrong value.

goal.data: Build the record, then project it, so the original name comes back out.

goal.spellcraft: Weave the blend, then draw it, so the original light comes back.
goal.abstract: Recover the A-component through a pairing then a projection.

afterSuccess.data: You built the record in the right order, then projected the first field — and the original name came back. The swapped builder put the age first, so the projection returned the wrong value; the mis-projection failed outright. A product's pairing and projections only fit together when they agree: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You combined in order, then drew the first part — the original salt came back. The swapped combiner and the mis-draw failed. Pairing and projection only fit when they agree: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You wove in order, then drew the first part — the original light came back. The swapped weaver and the mis-draw failed. Pairing and projection only fit when they agree: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f.
afterSuccess.abstract: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f: the faithful pairing followed by the first projection recovered the A-component. Swapping the pairing or mis-projecting breaks the law.

reveal.summary: The product's universal property ties pairing and projection together: π₁ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = f and π₂ ∘ ⟨f,g⟩ = g. Build a pair in order, and each projection reads its component back.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: fst({ a, b }) === a — when you build the tuple in the right order.
